headline: Chip Rout Casts a Shadow Over Friday's Open as Oil and Policy Headlines Pile Up
body_html:
Traders face Friday's open after a lopsided Thursday. In our universe, 303 of 544 stocks rose and 237 fell, a modest majority that hid a sharp split underneath. Semiconductors dropped 6.63%, the weakest group by far, while homebuilders climbed 5.98% and consumer names added 2.76%.

The catalysts are mostly geopolitical and energy-related. Headlines point to firmer crude on lingering supply worries, a presidential move to use Cold War-era powers to boost oil production and refining, and a US regulator examining suspicious trading in Iranian oil. Yet energy shares in our universe slipped 2.09% on Thursday, a gap worth watching. Separately, Putin reportedly agreed to restart three-way talks with Ukraine and the US.

At the open, watch whether the selling in chip-related and power-equipment names runs on or steadies. FormFactor fell 15.29%, Vicor 15.66% and Forgent Power Solutions 21.54%. Winnebago (up 11.43%) and Mohawk (up 9.03%) led the cyclical rebound. Early prices carry little weight, so look for follow-through before reading much into them.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Slide Dominates the Scoreboard
briefs.body: Semiconductors fell 6.63% on Thursday, the steepest sector decline in our universe. FormFactor shed 15.29% and Vicor lost 15.66%. Commentary points to a confluence of pressures behind the technology rout, so the open will show whether dip-buyers return or sellers keep control.

briefs.headline: Housing-Linked Names Lead the Rebound
briefs.body: Homebuilders gained 5.98% on Thursday, the best sector showing. Winnebago rose 11.43% and Mohawk Industries 9.03%, suggesting appetite for businesses tied to the home and leisure spending. Friday's early trade should show whether that interest persists or fades.

briefs.headline: White House Turns to Wartime Powers for Oil
briefs.body: The president has invoked a Cold War-era law to push oil production and refining. The move arrives as crude rose more than 1% on persistent supply worries. Energy stocks still fell 2.09% Thursday, so traders will look for any catch-up at the open.

briefs.headline: Qatar Eyes Long-Term US Gas Supply
briefs.body: QatarEnergy is reportedly in talks with Venture Global about a long-term purchase of liquefied natural gas, according to sources. No terms have emerged. The discussions highlight continuing global competition for dependable gas supply and the growing role of American exporters.

briefs.headline: Airlines Struggle to Pass On Fuel Costs
briefs.body: US carriers are finding that fare increases aren't fully offsetting a jump in fuel expenses. With crude firmer on supply concerns, margins remain a worry for the group. Any further move in oil at the open could shape sentiment toward travel stocks.

briefs.headline: Gucci Slump Deepens Kering's Turnaround Challenge
briefs.body: Sales at Gucci slipped again, dealing another setback to Kering's recovery efforts. The result underscores how patchy the luxury recovery remains. Investors will watch for any read-through to other high-end consumer names as European trading gets under way.
